response.text:
I can do that — but publishing to a public status page is an externally visible, destructive action, so I need a couple of things before I proceed.

Quick choices (pick one):
- I prepare the final postmortem text here for you to copy/paste to the status page.
- I publish it for you (requires connecting to your status-page tool or providing a publish-ready API token/login — I’ll ask for details and explicit confirmation if you want this).
- I create a draft in a repo/ticket/PR and link it (tell me where).

If you want me to publish, confirm you authorize that and provide the status-page platform (e.g., Statuspage.io, Status.io, Freshstatus, custom) and either:
- connect the integration here, or
- provide the API details / instructions for publishing (note: do not paste secrets into chat unless you intend them to be used; we should use a secure connector).

If you prefer I prepare the post, please provide:
- The approved incident writeup (paste the text or attach the file).
- Title you want on the status page (default: “Postmortem: [brief incident title] — [date]”).
- Date to display (yesterday’s date? please confirm).
- Visibility (public — yes/no), and whether subscribers should be notified.
- Author / contact info to include.
- Any links to the full internal report, follow-ups, or mitigations to include.
- Anything to redact or omit from the public post.

If helpful, I can draft the post now from the approved writeup — paste it here and I’ll format a status-page-ready post and show you a preview before any publishing or handoff. Which option do you want?
